newsitem.title: USA: Dow zigzags higher as price data renews rate doubt.
newsitem.headline: Dow zigzags higher as price data renews rate doubt.

text.p: Wall Street stocks whipsawed higher on Friday in a choppy session that saw new questions raised about the outlook for inflation and interest rates.
The Dow industrials rose 57 points to close unofficially at 6935, recouping slightly more than a third of the 160-point tumble suffered by the blue chip average on Thursday.

Stocks rallied sharply in the early stages of the session, sparked by a report that wholesale prices fell surprisingly sharply in February. The data reignited a raging debate on Wall Street about the threat of inflation in the economy.
Tobacco stocks recouped some of their losses from a day ago, with Philip Morris Cos Inc rising three points to 129 and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp rising 5/8 to 33-7/8.

But the story of the session was a 0.4 percent decline in the February Producer Price Index (PPI), which far outstripped the 0.1 percent dip forecast by economists. The index's core rate, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, fell by 0.1 percent, compared with forecasts for a 0.1 percent increase. The soft tone to the data reinvigorated stocks, which had sold off heavily on Thursday on the view that an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve was imminent.
"I think everyone backpedalled a bit today," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "It means we start next week with a much higher than usual level of uncertainty."

Despite the market friendly data, analysts said Federal Reserve policy remained an open question, noting recent comments by central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan focused on the need to quash future rather than current inflation risks.
But the severity of yesterday's sell-off, analysts said, meant the market had room to advance even without a clear green light on the interest rate front.
That sell-off was triggered by an unexpected surge in U.S. retail sales. While the rise suggested a surprisingly robust economy, analysts said the market's reaction was overblown.

"The data we saw yesterday didn't warrant a 160-point drop," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "But a lot of that may have been people anticipating a sloppy PPI and we certainly didn't get that."
With the Fed meeting still more than a week away, analysts said the market was unlikely to depart from its volatile ways anytime soon.

"Any sign of economic weakness will be taken as a temporary reason to rally," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates. "But it's all going to come down to what happens on the 25th."
The Dow's gains on the day trimmed its loss for the week to 65.43 points. The S&P 500 rose 3.61 points to 793.17 and the New York Stock Exchange Composite rose 1.83 to 417.70.
Technology stocks were unable to hold onto their early gains, however, leaving the Nasdaq Composite with a fractional loss. The index fell 0.31 of a point to 1292.97.
In individual issues, Aplied Magnetics Corp fell 1-7/8 to 31-3/8 after abandoning its hostile attempt to acquire Read-Rite Corp. Shares in Read-Rite fell 3-1/8 to 26-5/8.

Employee Solutions Inc slid 9-1/8 to 6-1/4, extending a slide that started yesterday, when the company said delayed release of its fourth quarter results. Today it said its earnings for the period would be below analysts' estimates.
Fluor Corp fell fell 6-3/4 to 57-3/4. Several Wall Street firms downgraded the shares today.
Oracle Corp jumped 4-7/8 to 41. Late yesterday, the company reported stronger than expected third quarter earnings.
